# SK3003 — Configure awaited tasks in library code

<!-- Generated from Rules/Rikarin.Skala.Rules.Metadata/rules.json. Do not edit. -->

A bare framework Task or ValueTask is awaited where EditorConfig explicitly selects library ConfigureAwait analysis.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | Async |
| Default severity | warning |
| Scope | Semantic |
| Needs a compilation | yes |
| Fix | no |
| Language version floor | — |
| Since | 1.3 |

## Why

Library code can choose not to capture its caller's synchronization context. The existing resharper_configure_await_analysis_mode policy determines whether this inspection applies; disabled, missing, invalid and UI mode do not require missing configuration. Explicit ConfigureAwait choices are respected. Scheduling policy is an author decision, so this rule reports without an automatic fix.

## Example

Instead of:

```csharp
// resharper_configure_await_analysis_mode = library
await ReadAsync();
```

Write:

```csharp
await ReadAsync().ConfigureAwait(false);
```

## When it does not fire

Only exact framework Task, Task<T>, ValueTask and ValueTask<T> awaits are included. Derived task types and custom awaitables are excluded. Already configured awaitables, including explicit true or variable arguments, are left alone. UI mode's redundant ConfigureAwait(true) inspection is not SK3003 and is not implemented here. await foreach and await using are outside the initial scope. The prefixed configuration key wins when both spellings exist.

## Configuration

- `resharper_configure_await_analysis_mode`
- `configure_await_analysis_mode`
- `dotnet_diagnostic.SK3003.severity`
